commits.message:
Correct a count I inflated by hand: three rebuilds, not four

The prompt table was rebuilt from the run's own tool rows, and in the
paraphrase I wrote "rebuilt the pods four times". The tool rows contain three
`Rebuild ...` calls and one initial build. Counting them takes one grep:

    'Rebuild 4 RCS cassettes flush-mounted with 5 exposed nozzles each'
    'Rebuild RCS cassettes with corrected X placement'
    'Rebuild brackets for hull-flank and wingtip cassettes'

This is the exact failure the rest of the README exists to avoid: the numbers
that came from the capture are right, and the one I typed by hand was wrong.
Found while writing about the project, not by reading it.

Use the take the owner preferred, and re-derive every number from it

The owner asked for another roll of the dice and to see both. The first attempt
came back ugly - a tall dorsal fin standing out of the middle of the hull and a
grey ribbed canister stuck to the side - and was stopped mid-flight at turn 2
rather than left to burn fifteen more minutes on a rejected ship. The rerun, on
prompts the owner shortened themselves while the first run was still going,
produced a dark stealth interceptor they preferred, so that is what ships.

Nothing was deleted to make room. The previous video stays in issue #1 as its
own comment, so its asset URL is still live and this is revertible in one line.

Every number is re-derived from the new run rather than edited in place, because
a half-updated table is worse than an obviously wrong one:

    1278 s   -> 917 s (15 min)      56 calls -> 52, 4 read-only (was 8)
    194,113  -> 109,016 tokens      cache 97% -> 98%
    objects 25 -> 43                objects 17 -> 18, MESH 12 -> 13
    "cut to 17 s" -> 18 s           "21 minutes" -> 15 minutes

The prompt table now quotes what the harness actually sent - the owner's
shortened prompts 1 and 4 - and the "what came back" column is rebuilt from the
run's own tool rows instead of paraphrased, which is why it can say the model
ray-cast every RCS nozzle to prove the exhaust path was clear.

One caveat is dead rather than restated. The old README admitted its flight was
timed off Blender's assumed 24 fps; this take logs `scene fps: 24`, so the
playback rate is measured. Same number, but it stops being a guess.

`tools/demo_capture.py` goes in with it, because the README now claims those
prompts are what the harness sends and the file has to agree.

Verified: the video URL is a bare URL alone on its own paragraph (the only form
GitHub renders as a player rather than a broken image), all six local assets
resolve, no stale figure from the old take survives a grep, the manifest still
validates, and 4 CPython suites are green.

Stop claiming a licence, and say what the licence key actually is

The README carried a `licence-GPL-3.0-or-later` badge and a closing line
asserting it as fact, while no LICENSE file existed anywhere in the repo. A
claim to the world with nothing behind it is worse than no claim, so both are
gone, and the closing line now says the true thing: no terms have been chosen,
so nothing here is licensed for reuse yet.

The manifest could not be treated the same way, and that is measured rather
than assumed. Deleting the `license` key fails:

    Error parsing TOML "blender_manifest.toml"
    missing "license"

so the key stays - it is a value the platform *requires*, not a grant the
author has made. The comment above it now says exactly that, cites the command
that proves it, and no longer reads as a placeholder "revisit before any
distribution" when this is already distributed.

README oomph, kept inside the voice the project already had, because hype that
contradicts "verify, don't assert" would undercut the one thing this README is
for:

  * a hook that states the result rather than the category - "Five sentences
    in. A spaceship out." - and names what it is not (no bridge, no sidecar);
  * a three-line "why it is different" up top, including the guard that was
    NOT built because its own probe showed it does not contain;
  * a star call to action and a keyword line, plus two badges replacing the
    licence one.

Discovery is mostly repo metadata, not prose: the description still read
"(demo media)" from when this repo held only a video, and there were zero
topics. Now 20 topics (blender, bpy, ai-agents, llm-agent, deepseek,
tool-use, ...) and a description that says what the thing does.

Verified: `blender -c extension validate` still prints "Success parsing TOML";
0 licence badges remain; the only licence mentions left in the README are the
disclaimers themselves; markdown inside the footer's <sub> does render as
markup on GitHub (<strong>/<code>), checked against the live page rather than
assumed.

Record the demo live, and let the animation finish playing The README claimed an assistant that drives Blender, and illustrated it with a scripted walk-through. A demo that mocks the headline feature is not evidence for the headline feature, so the demo now runs the real thing: the owner's five prompts, the real `transport.Worker`, the real provider, no key and no network only when DEMO_LIVE is unset. Two bugs in the recording were found by measuring rather than by looking, and both had the same shape - a pipeline quietly discarding work: * The composer's static-frame pruner dropped 86 of 241 flight frames. Its threshold is tuned for the panel, where one sentence arriving changes many pixels; at the 160x100 the metric downsamples to, a smoothly moving ship changes fewer, so a continuous animation was being deleted as a static screen. Flight frames are now never pruned. * Joining the two segments with `-c copy` collapsed them into a single 15 fps stream, so the flight played slower than it was authored. The concat filter is used instead, and ffprobe confirms 22.43s = 12.4s of build + 241 flight frames at 24 fps. The filming harness also had to stop photographing things it should not: the default cube sat inside the hull until `clear_scene()`, and a crashed run auto-saved the preferences it had set, which is why `poll()` now restores them around any exception and DEMO_CRASH_AT exists to test that path. The video is hosted as a GitHub asset URL rather than in this repository. The URL renders as a

Make the round cap a lever, without moving the designed 8

The owner asked why a turn stopped after 8 rounds: a six-part detail pass
(nacelle pylons, nose sensor booms, dorsal rails, ventral skids, blades,
marker lights) had hit MAX_ROUNDS mid-work and needed a second
`Send "continue"`. The cap is real and deliberate - ticket 09 §1 reasoned
that a normal ask is 2-4 rounds, so 8 allows one self-repair - but it was a
constant, and the two reasons it gave have both weakened: the projection now
trims history to fit a budget derived from the window, so context is not the
binding constraint, and a long modelling job is exactly the case that
outgrows a fixed number.

So the cap is now readable through an injected hook - `Conversation.
round_source`, wired by `stream.rounds_per_turn` to a `rounds_per_turn`
preference (0 = the designed 8, ceiling 64) - and the stop message quotes
the cap that actually applied. The DEFAULT IS UNCHANGED: nobody's ratified
behaviour moves unless they ask for it.

`context_history_kib` was not drawn anywhere either, so the preferences page
gained a "Limits" box carrying both caps. A lever nothing reaches is not a
lever: that field was read for a whole ticket's worth of work while being
unreachable except by knowing the RNA name.

Checked: a preference of 11 takes 10 requests and the message says "11
rounds"; 0, a missing preference, one that raises, and one that is not a
number all fall back to the designed 8 (a mistyped preference must not stop
a turn); unwired, the designed default runs. Plus the existing cap checks,
and prefs_draw_smoke now pins both fields being drawn.

commits.message: Release v1.4.0

Worktrees, update notifications, AI changelog, single instance, tests

- Worktrees section: finds git worktrees across code folders and agent
  working folders; verdicts Already on main / Branch deleted on GitHub /
  Probably done / Keep (changes, in use, locked, active) / Missing. Checks
  and sizes fill in progressively, 8 at a time. Remove one or clean up all
  safe ones; never --force (git refuses uncommitted work), branches kept,
  in-use re-checked at click time. leftovers --worktrees [--json].
- Merged means merged into local main OR origin/main (git 2.48+ creates
  origin/HEAD on fetch, so local-only merges were missed before).
- Updates: a notification when an update is ready (Settings toggle), an
  Update Available menu item, What's New links; failures logged to
  ~/Library/Logs/Leftovers/updates.log; --install restores the user's
  auto-download setting.
- CHANGELOG.md written by Claude from each release's commits (plain words,
  5 short bullets); release.sh generates notes for GitHub and the update
  window. Backfilled 1.0.0-1.3.0.
- Only one copy runs at a time; --help and unknown flags never start the
  app; install-local keeps a single installed copy.
- Tests (Swift Testing): 23 tests including real-git integration.

Understand English relative time phrases, and make the timezone configurable

Relative time phrases were parsed in Japanese only, so an English
"yesterday" fell through as a plain search keyword. Day boundaries were
also hardcoded to JST, so "yesterday" was cut at Japan's midnight for
everyone.

- index_exact: English dates (today, yesterday, the day before
  yesterday, last night, N days/weeks/months/years ago with digits or
  number words, last week/month/year, the month/year before last,
  "in July", "July 19", "19th of July") and times of day (morning,
  afternoon, evening, night, late night, noon, "around 3pm", "9 am"),
  with the same meanings as the Japanese rules. A month name alone
  counts only after "in"/"during", so "may" and "march" are never
  read as dates. Greetings ("good morning", "goodnight") are not times.
- Time phrases are blanked out before keyword extraction, and English
  stopwords are checked per token (never substring-replaced), so
  "what did we say yesterday about the budget" searches for "budget"
  inside yesterday.
- In-range keyword matching is case-insensitive.
- "the first time", "last time", "back then" widen the range like
  their Japanese counterparts.
- config "timezone" (IANA name, e.g. "America/New_York"); unset means
  this machine's local time. Used for parsing, day bucketing in
  ingest, display in recall, and the LLL index. tzdata is added on
  Windows.
- tests/test_time_words.py: 34 new cases with "now" pinned, including
  an end-to-end recall in New York time and a check that Japanese is
  unchanged in Tokyo time. All 39 tests pass.

Hand-written word lists instead of dateparser: its search mode returns
points rather than ranges and fires on ordinary words; a fixed
vocabulary is predictable and testable.

commits.message:
test(melpa): preload jka-compr before the source-only load suffixes

The parity startup form sets `load-suffixes '(".el")` so a package is read
as source, but an INSTALLED GNU ships its Lisp compressed (`make install`
runs the sources through GZIP_PROG: `pcase.el.gz`), so the first `require`
of an editor library reached for `jka-compr.el.gz` to decompress itself
and GNU signaled `Recursive load`.  Every MELPA batch died during
RestartProbe with exit 255; a local build tree hid it because its lisp is
plain `.el`.

The form now requires `jka-compr` before narrowing the suffixes.  It
loads through the default suffixes (`jka-compr.elc` when installed, a
no-op in a build tree) and neomacs requires it fine.  Contract tests pin
the order and that the Emacs-default policy still touches neither.

Verified against an installed pinned GNU (a local `make install` to the
configured prefix, gzipped lisp): the pre-fix shape reproduces the
Recursive load by hand, and the a/aas/abc_mode batches -- including one
with its package cache removed -- pass with the fix.

test(parity): resolve the checked-in pin from the live workspace

manifest_path() read env!("CARGO_WORKSPACE_DIR") at runtime, so on every
archived shard the melpa-test-support preflight asked for
/home/ubuntu/work/neomacs/neomacs/parity-reference.toml -- the archive
build machine's path -- and all tui shards and MELPA jobs failed right
after the oracle setup started passing.  The crate's test helpers read
the same constant; all three sites now use
neomacs_infra::workspace_root(), with neomacs-infra added as a
dependency.

test(parity): attest the GNU release, not the build fingerprint

The pin records a RELEASE: the tag emacs-31.1, which the running editor
reports as `emacs-version`.  That is the only identity an installed GNU
can prove -- `emacs-repository-version` is computed by running git in
`source-directory` (lisp/version.el), which `make install` does not
create -- and GNU's own fingerprint hashes the temacs executable, so a
rebuild on another toolchain changes it while the source stays put.
CI's oracle is built by the workflow's action, so every tui shard and
MELPA job refused it ("pinned 65a0d3fc / found 4c83a960") as soon as the
installed-layout probe could find the dump at all.

Both readers now verify the dump magic -- which is also what tells a
non-GNU peer from a GNU before `--if-gnu` would have to run it -- and the
release version the editor reports.  The fingerprint, mirror commit and
SHA-256/size fields stay in the manifest as provenance recorded by
pin-reference, and the two depths are kept for the API and the stamp.
Fixtures are now scripts that report a controlled version, and the
sensitivity tests plant another release.

Verified against the pinned mirror: the build tree, a simulated
`make install` prefix, `--if-gnu` on the port, and
scripts/melpa-infra-preflight.sh end to end.

test: resolve CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR at runtime in the remaining archived suites

Same class as the neovm-core fix: fixture roots, weston configs and
source-probe paths read env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") at runtime, which
names the build machine's path.  Oracle autoload/load-suffix fixtures,
display protocol and runtime witness tests, gui tests, renderer tests,
the MELPA process-wait audit, terminfo and the perf architecture test
now use neomacs_infra::crate_root!(); crates that lacked the dependency
gained it as a dev-dependency.

test(neovm-core): resolve fixture roots at runtime in the archived tests

compat_module_semantics told cargo to build a test cdylib with its
current_dir under the compile-time manifest path, so on a shard whose
workspace is a different path the spawn failed with ENOENT and every
module test in the package went red.  The architecture layout scans, the
bytecode source probes and the tagged gc.rs line-ceiling read the same
dead path.  All now go through neomacs_infra::crate_root!(), with
neomacs-infra added as a dev-dependency.

commits.message:
fix(elasticache): support HELLO AUTH handshakes (#4476)

* fix(elasticache): support HELLO AUTH handshakes

* fix(elasticache): bound HELLO handshake retries

feat(iam): add last-accessed reporting actions (#4488)

Add GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails, GetServiceLastAccessedDetails,
GetServiceLastAccessedDetailsWithEntities and ListPoliciesGrantingServiceAccess.

Floci records no service-access history, but AWS's "never used" shape keeps
the report and nulls the usage fields rather than emptying the report, so
that is what these reproduce. GetServiceLastAccessedDetails lists every
service the entity could reach through its permissions policies and leaves
LastAuthenticated and TotalAuthenticatedEntities absent for the ones never
used. GetServiceLastAccessedDetailsWithEntities lists the entities that
could have used the reported permissions: a group report yields the group's
users, a policy report the users and roles it is attached to, and a user or
role report that entity. Both lists come from permissions-policy logic,
which Floci can evaluate, so both are computed rather than stubbed; the
usage timestamps are the only part left out.

A report is produced when the job is created and stored with it, matching
AWS, where the Get operations retrieve a report that Generate produced. So
editing the policies afterwards does not change what a completed job
answers, and deleting the entity does not stop a valid JobId resolving.
Generate resolves the whole ARN first, rejecting one whose account is not
the caller's or whose path is not the resolved entity's, so it cannot fall
back to a same-named local identity; AWS-managed policy ARNs carry the
literal "aws" account and are allowed through to the global catalog. An
unknown JobId is NoSuchEntity, Granularity is validated and echoed back as
JobType, and both readers honour MaxItems and Marker.

ListPoliciesGrantingServiceAccess needs no job and no usage history, since
AWS defines it purely over permissions-policy logic. A user contributes its
own managed and inline policies plus those of every group it belongs to,
while a group or role contributes only its own; permissions boundaries are
excluded. Only Allow grants, and Allow with NotAction grants every service
the list does not carve out. It models a Marker but no MaxItems, so only the
former is applied.

Services reachable only through a wildcard or NotAction cannot be
enumerated without a catalog of IAM service namespaces, which is tracked
separately in #4487 and documented.

fix(s3): apply AWS's CreateBucket region rules in every partition (#4494)

* fix(s3): apply AWS's CreateBucket region rules in every partition

CreateBucket follows the rules moto verified against AWS: the us-east-1 endpoint takes any LocationConstraint but its own (InvalidLocationConstraint), and every other regional endpoint requires a constraint naming exactly its region, answering IllegalLocationConstraintException otherwise. The signing region alone no longer places a bucket, so a China or GovCloud client must send the constraint, which the AWS SDKs do. GetBucketLocation still answers an empty constraint only for us-east-1, in every partition.

WAF's CLOUDFRONT scope lives in the partition's implicit global region and is refused with WAFInvalidParameterException where the partition has no CloudFront. Lightsail lists no regions outside the commercial partition. Region fallbacks read the configured default where a resolver or config is in scope, and PreSignedUrlGenerator gains an overload that signs for a given region. The region-literal category of the partition guardrail is now gated; every remaining literal carries a stated reason.

Tests that created buckets under a regional signing scope with no constraint now send one, and S3IntegrationTest's case that pinned the old signing-region placement is replaced by the rejection and its positive twin.

Part of #4272

* fix(s3,wafv2): answer a us-east-1 constraint off its endpoint as a mismatch, and gate the CLOUDFRONT scope on every operation

A CreateBucket on a regional endpoint other than us-east-1 with LocationConstraint us-east-1 is just another mismatched region, IllegalLocationConstraintException, as moto's aws_verified test_create_bucket_with_wrong_location_constraint records; InvalidLocationConstraint belongs to the us-east-1 endpoint alone (test_bucket_create_force_us_east_1). The body parse no longer rejects us-east-1 early, and bucketRegionForCreate checks the endpoint mismatch first.

WAF's CLOUDFRONT scope was refused in partitions without CloudFront only when creating a resource; validateScope, which every operation already calls, now applies the same check, so a List or Get for that scope answers the same WAFInvalidParameterException.

* fix(wafv2): check the CLOUDFRONT scope against the region each call is about

The previous change checked the scope in validateScope against the request region, but CloudFormation calls the service outside any request, where that region falls back to the deployment default: under a GovCloud default a commercial stack's CLOUDFRONT WebACL was refused on create, update and delete. WafV2Handler now checks Scope=CLOUDFRONT against the region the API request was sent to, before dispatch, so every operation still answers the same error; validateScope checks the enum only, and a create keeps its check against the region it is given where the ARN is built.

fix(kinesisanalytics): make the savepoints volume writable by the Flink user (#4490)

* fix(kinesisanalytics): make the savepoints volume writable by the Flink user

Docker creates the savepoints named volume root:root, while the official
apache/flink images run Flink as uid/gid 9999, so the JobManager could not
create /opt/flink/savepoints and every CreateApplicationSnapshot ended
FAILED. Initialise the volume root through
ContainerLifecycleManager.ensureSharedVolume, chowning it to 9999:9999
before the JobManager starts.

Closes #4443

* fix(core): reinitialise shared volume ownership when the volume is recreated

ensureSharedVolume memoised the one-off chown per volume name for the
whole process, so a volume removed and recreated under the same name
(DeleteApplication in memory mode, or docker volume rm) came back
root:root without being initialised again. Drop the memo whenever the
volume has just been created.

feat(route53): resolve private hosted zone records from cluster containers (#4353)

Implement DnsRecordSource SPI via Route53DnsRecordSource to decouple Route 53 resolution from EmbeddedDnsServer. Add DnsLookupHelper in core.common.dns for external IPv4 resolution via upstream forwarders with system fallback, shared by Route53DnsRecordSource for CNAME and ALIAS chasing. Discover private hosted zones via Route53Service and support in-zone chasing, built-in Floci suffixes, and EC2 internal names. Authoritatively resolve A records within private zones to prevent upstream query leakage. Wire EKS cluster containers to embedded DNS via specBuilder.withEmbeddedDns().

edges that turn back no longer cross each other or their own node

Two edges looping over the same row used to be drawn on top of each
other; they now nest, the shorter inside. An edge whose sides are at a
right angle, such as from: left  to: top, used to cut back across its
own node; it now goes around, over or under as its far side says.

one edge may pass some nodes above or below and others left or right

An edge could say below m or left of n, but not both. It now can: the
line turns between the two as often as its clauses need, across first
unless a side named at an end says otherwise.

commits.message:
Refresh screenshots for 2.4; let desktop widgets pass the cover check

The capture check refused every run on a Mac with desktop widgets: they
are Notification Center windows at desktop level, a negative layer, and
the front-to-back walk reached them before the backdrop. Windows below
layer 0 can never cover an app window, so the walk now skips them. The
General and Settings screenshots are recaptured and show version 2.4.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bump the Homebrew cask on each release

A tag build now points Casks/translate-like-me.rb in wiltodelta/homebrew-tap
at the new release: the build job exports the zip's sha256, and a homebrew job
commits the new version and checksum through a write deploy key scoped to the
tap. It runs in this workflow because a release made with GITHUB_TOKEN starts
no other workflow. The README gains the brew install command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Give each language pair its own writing style

A pair's style applies only to its translations, and two pairs may share
languages, so one can carry the user's voice and another translate someone
else's text plainly. The style is edited in a sheet from the pair's row, so a
long voice guide never grows the settings pane. At launch the earlier global
style moves into the pairs when none has a style yet, and is then removed.

The status menu tells same-language pairs apart with a subtitle. The swap
button is gone: the direction is detected per translation, and the order
only picks the target for text in neither language.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Refresh the README and title releases from the tag annotation

The README drops the stale 'always the latest model' claim and a clipboard
note the Privacy section already makes, says the API keys are keychain items in
the bundle-identifier section, explains a missing Effort picker, and adds an
Uninstall section. CI now titles each release with the annotation's first line.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Update in place with Sparkle; harden privacy, clipboard and CI

Sparkle 2 replaces the check-and-notify updater: a daily check against the
EdDSA-signed appcast each release publishes, with gentle reminders so a
scheduled find never takes focus (the menu item becomes "Install Update…").
build.sh embeds and signs the framework; CI generates the signed appcast and
takes the release notes from the tag annotation, refusing a tag without them.

Privacy and safety from an audit: API keys move to the keychain (plain-text
copies are migrated and removed); claude and codex run without session
history; codex runs read-only with its tools disabled and gets the prompt on
stdin; a CLI failure shows and logs only its error lines, never the echoed
selection; the clipboard is restored with every type it held, left alone if
the user copied meanwhile, and the pasted translation is marked transient.

Also: strict SwiftLint locally and in CI, os.Logger throughout, launch-at-login
failures shown in Settings, Grok's default model read from `grok models` so
Settings names it and offers Effort, the dead modal-alert guard removed,
absolute actool paths (the agent resolved relative ones against another
checkout, which explains the stray Resources/Assets.plist), pinned actions and
a keychain locked after notarization.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
